args.query: Gullwick Saltmere Tarred Gull Sela Bram

properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman at Gullwick Docks; the only one who rows near the bell water
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, never looks anyone in the eye, keeps her gaze on the tide line; mends a net, shrugs, curt
properties.wants: Never to be on the water at night
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, forty years ago; her grandmother said the water came up warm

sources.quote: She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.
Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced; the GM keeps the spelling Sela.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Where the table left her.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, gulls; the far piers are rotting. By day the fog still sits on the docks and gulls are everywhere; pier four is where boats can be found.

sources.quote: The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: The GM's new description of the docks.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago on the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Sela ties the mine's flooding to the bell's origin.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about the mine.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. About an hour's walk. The entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side. Warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. Thirty paces in the tunnel floods with warm black water; wet hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: What the players saw in the mine.

properties.what_changed: A hymn-book page in Saltmere Mine has "M. Brand" pencilled in the margin; Teo says it is Mira's handwriting.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".
That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: First physical trace of Mira; the GM did not confirm the handwriting.

change.name: Is Maren Vosk in the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master is behind the choir; nothing at the table supports it yet.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Player theory, kept as a thread and not as fact.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: just the bell tower and two broken arches, with seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water.

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows.

changes.why: What the players saw at the chapel.

properties.statement: Fishermen say a Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Local rumor; the GM did not confirm it.

properties.statement: When the bell rings at midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the drowned chapel floor like a congregation, then vanish when it stops.

sources.quote: Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation. Then the bell stops and they're gone.

changes.why: First sight of the drowned congregation.

sources.quote: standing on the chapel floor under the water

changes.why: The fact is about the chapel.

sources.quote: And then, right at midnight, the bell rings again under the water. Twelve times. And the humming is back, but louder.
(to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.

changes.why: The bell rang again and the GM set the clock to three of six.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks. Fire going; it smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New place the party sleeps at.

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks; friendly, feeds the party for free
properties.knows: Has known Maren Vosk for thirty years; says she lost a brother to the bay

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He runs the inn.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Bram's account of Maren's past.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: The fact is about Maren.

properties.what_is_open: The party wants to follow Mira's hymn-book trail to the chapel, where they think the hymns came from.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four at first light, row out, and dive to the chapel at low tide; Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.
properties.deadline: First light tomorrow; Sela rows by day only

sources.quote: Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.
So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.

changes.why: The party's plan for next session.

sources.quote: Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: The plan targets the chapel.
